Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session on Day 2 of this second Test. The two English openers Dom Sibley and Zak Crawley are out in the middle. The Sri Lankan Players too are in readiness. Suranga Lakmal to start the proceedings with the ball then for the Lankans. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

Right then, England have more than an anticipated task at hand. They would feel that they have conceded 100 or so runs extra. And for them to do well in this game, further, they will count on their openers to get them off to a good start. Both Sibley and Crawley did not have a great outing in the first Test and would be looking to make amends here. Join us for the final session (and for England's response) shortly...

Then, some further excellent rearguard action from the Lankans saw them get to 381, when at one point, it was deemed that 275 was all they could get. It was the seamers all the way, for England, and within that, it was an Anderson show. When he got Dickwella, he got his 33rd fifer in Tests and went onto take 6 wickets overall. Wood got three and Curran got the last wicket. Nothing for the English spinners but we can expect spin to play a proper role from now on.

Sri Lanka had won the toss earlier and opted to bat first. And the way they got off to a start, it looked like a repeat of the first innings of the first Test match was on the cards. But two important partnerships, between Mathews and Thirimanne, and Mathews and Chandimal, set the Sri Lankan ship back on track. Angelo Mathews would himself go onto make a hundred before falling. And then, Dickwella batted well but fell 8 runs shy of his maiden Test hundred.

A very handy 67 from Perera and Sri Lanka finish on 381. England have picked all the 10 wickets and all of them, surprisingly, have gone to the seamers. This has happened for the first time in Galle. The tired English bodies would be happy as they make their way back.

OUT! CAUGHT! Finally the last wicket falls! Sam Curran also has a wicket to his name! Perera has played a wonderful knock and has taken Sri Lanka to 381. Short ball on middle, Perera pulls it to deep square leg. Leach runs across, slides and takes a very good catch. SRI LANKA ALL OUT FOR 381.
FOUR! More like it! This was hammered! Full toss on middle, Perera hammers it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Low full toss on off, Perera drives it to deep point and refuses to take the single.
Very full ball outside off, Perera digs it out to deep point for a single.
Fullish ball on off, Perera solidly defends it out.
Full ball on off, Perera defends it to cover.
Good length ball outside off, pushed to cover.
Good length ball on middle, Dilruwan nudges it to mid-wicket.
Slower ball on off, Perera waits for it and then defends it out.
Good length ball on off, Fernando survives as he taps it to gully.
Good length ball on middle, Fernando works it to mid-wicket.
EDGY! Good length ball on off, Perera looks to defend but it takes the outside edge and it goes to the third man region for a single. Asitha Fernando has two balls to face in this over.
Short ball on middle, Perera ducks under it.
Short of a length ball outside off, Perera punches it to deep point and refuses to take the single.
Good length ball on off, Perera pushes it to the mid-wicket region.
This should have been the scheduled Tea break but since it is the last wicket, the session has been extended for 30 minutes.
On middle, clipped behind square on the on side for a single.
FOUR! Just using the pace here. Very full and outside off, Perera digs it out nicely, past Joe Root at point, and gets a boundary here.
WIDE! Another slower short one, outside off, Asitha lets it be. 2 bouncers for the over and hence it is called a wide here.
Short and around off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short length ball, slower as well, on top of the stumps. Dilruwan Perera is not interested in playing at that. Lets it through as he sways away.
Short length delivery, outside off, Perera lets that one be.
Shortish length ball around off, Dilruwan pulls it to deep mid-wicket but for no runs.
Full length ball outside off, defended to the off side.
Angles in a shortish length delivery around the off stump, defended to the off side by Fernando.
Fullish length delivery outside the off pole line, Asitha pokes it towards gully, who dives and stops it.
Well outside off and AF has no business in fiddling with that. Lets it be.
Full length delivery outside off, Asitha Fernando is able to defend it to the off side.
Full length delivery, well outside the off pole, Fernando lets that be.
Sam Curran is back on. 16-2-55-0 are his figures so far.
Short ball around middle, Perera ducks underneath it. 4 runs from the over.
Mark Wood comes in from wide of the crease and angles it on middle and leg, clipped to square leg.
This one is down the leg side and he shoulders arms.
DP moves to the leg side and Wood follows him with a back of a length delivery. Dilruwan dabs it on the off side.
Short length ball around middle, Dilruwan sits under that one. The field is well set for short deliveries. How long can Perera resist, to not have a go?

FOUR! Looks like Dilruwan Perera has decided to step on the gas here. Three fielders on the on side but nobody had a chance. Full and on the middle pole, Perera just picks it up and dismisses it to the long leg ropes.
Asitha safely sees off this over. Full length delivery, Fernando defends it out to the off side.
Fuller in length and around off, tapped to the off side.

PUT DOWN! But that was ferociously hit. Full and on middle, Perera skips down the track and whacks it powerfully back to Bess. The offie looks to take it but the power with which it was hit ensures that the ball goes through his hands. A single sneaked in here. Bess looks to be in some trouble here. But he is fine to continue now.
On off and middle, pushed back to Dom.
Flatter ball on the pads, Dilruwan goes back and wears it on his pads.

Off the footmarks that! Bess lands it down the leg side, it pitches and goes down further. Buttler looks to stop that but he fails to do so. Joe Root, behind Buttler, does well to stop that and save some blushes for Buttler there.
Asitha Fernando is the last man in.

OUT! TAKEN! But this time, the outside edge is generated and is taken. Length and outside the off pole, Embuldeniya looks to drive it on the off side but ends up generating an outside edge there. Finally, one would reckon (or at least the visitors would). It goes to the English skipper at first slip who manages to hold onto it. You could see that Wood was letting the frustration go there, as he got the wicket. He was bowling his heart out to the left-hander and beating him previously, on the outside edge. This time, the outside edge is generated, it is taken, and Wood is a relieved man.
BEATEN! Well, another one which does not see the outside edge. Length ball outside off, Lasith Embuldeniya looks to play at that but gets beaten on the outside edge there.
Fuller in length ball on middle, Perera clips it through mid-wicket. Takes a single.
Fuller in length delivery, on off and middle, the right-hander blocks it to the off side.
Not timed by Dilruwan Perera. Full and on the middle pole line, DP flicks but Dom Bess, at square leg, keeps that one out.
Full ball on middle, nudged to the man at mid on.
Full delivery, Lasith Embuldeniya keeps it out on the off side. 363/8 are the Sri Lankans, at the end of 132 overs.
Full and on off and middle, Embuldeniya nudges it back to Bess.
Outside the off pole line, dabbed to the off side.
That is the line that an offspinner should be bowling to a left-hander. Full and on the off pole line, Lasith taps it to the man at silly point.
Full length ball on the off pole, blocked to the off side.
Bowls a very full length ball on off, it is jammed out to cover.
Dom Bess is back on. 24-1-75-0 are his figures so far.
It is well played. Mark runs in and bowls a length delivery, outside off, it pitches and seams back in sharply. Perera stands tall and defends it out.
Shortish and down the leg side, Dilruwan lets that one be.
Shortish length ball around the off pole line, defended back on the track.

FOUR! FIFTY FOR PERERA! His 7th in his Test career. It was a long time coming. Fullish length delivery on the middle pole, Dilruwan Perera turns it nicely to the leg side. Sam Curran, at fine leg, runs to his left and dives but fails to keep it out. A boundary results.

Off the thigh pad. Shortish length delivery on the body, Perera looks to flick but it comes straight off the thigh pad. The man at leg slip takes it but not much interest from the English. They too knew it came off the thigh.
Well bowled. Wood bowls a yorker on off and middle, it just tailed in a little. Dilruwan Perera did well to dig it out.
Full length delivery around the off stump line, blocked to the man at short leg.
Flatter and outside the off stump, Perera rocks back and clips it through mid-wicket. The batsmen cross. At the moment, singles are too easy for Sri Lanka.
Very full length delivery outside the off pole line, Embuldeniya comes down and digs it wide of the bowler. They cross for one.
On off, Lasith skips down the track and pushes it back to the spinner.
Down the wicket but not off the middle of the bat. Leach gives it more air and lands it full and around the off pole, Dilruwan dances down and lofts it over mid on. Gets just the single though.
Slower through the air and on off, blocked.

Time for the mandatory concussion check here, for Lasith Embuldeniya. The umpires check on him and ask the Sri Lankan physio to come out. The physio checks Embuldeniya and applies the magic spray on the left-hander. Right he looks good and set to resume again.

That was nasty from Wood! Wood bowls a bouncer on middle, Embuldeniya looks to duck but the ball does not rise as high as he expected. It hits him around the shoulder and then hits the helmet and lobs to point where it lands in front of the fielder.
Full ball on off, Embuldeniya defends it to cover.
Good length ball on the pads, Dilruwan flicks it to backward square leg and crosses over for a run.
Short ball around middle, Perera sits under it.
Good length ball on middle, Perera works it to square leg.
Full ball on middle, Dilruwan flicks it through the mid-wicket region and picks up a couple of runs before the fielder cuts it off.
This one is flatter and on the stumps, Embuldeniya camps back and taps it to the man at short leg to see off the over.
Better from Leach. Floated on off and middle, Lasith defends it.
SIX! Take that, says Embuldeniya. And he has helped the hosts register 350 on the board. A touch fuller, outside off, Embuldeniya gets down and mows a huge slog sweep over deep mid-wicket.
Flatter and on off, Embuldeniya taps it to the leg side.
Full and on the stumps, Lasith Embuldeniya comes down the track but ends up pushing it back to the bowler.
Flat and outside off, punched off the back foot, to sweeper cover, for a single.
And Embuldeniya survives the over. Very full and around off, Lasith jams it out to the off side for a dot.
BEATEN! Full length ball outside off, Lasith Embuldeniya hangs his bat out, looking to defend, but the ball whizzes past his outside edge.
Yorker, outside off, Lasith digs it out to the man at wide mid off. There was an easy run there but Perera was not interested in that.
Another short one and Embuldeniya has no issues in sitting under that one. This short ball though did not bounce much, like the previous ones.
Shortish and around off, Embuldeniya defends it to the man at mid off.
Bumper on top of the stumps, Lasith safely ducks under that one.

Drinks! England have done well since Lunch but they would want to take the remaining 2 wickets as quickly as possible. James Anderson has bowled very well again while they need more from their spinners. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, will be pleased and they would hope that Perera adds a few more runs on the board. They already have a good score on a wicket which is not going to get easier on the wicket. How many more runs will they add? Mark Wood is back into the attack.
No single. Flatter and outside off, Dilruwan Perera nudges it to the off side. Looks for a single but there was none there. So, Embuldeniya will take strike in the next over.
Blocks this fuller one to the off side.
Shorter and outside off, Perera goes back and fends it out on the off side.
Full and on the off pole, blocked to the off side.
Flatter ball outside off, Dilruwan defends it out.
Flighted outside off, Perera keeps it out.
Full and well outside off, Lasith looks to force it through the off side but he misses it.
Short and down the leg side, the left-hander lets it be.
Outside off, stabbed to the man at backward point.

Full and on off, Perera defends it solidly back to the bowler. Anderson takes the ball and tries to run out Lasith Embuldeniya at the other end but misses to hit the stumps. They steal a single off the overthrows there.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.
Full length ball around off, Dilruwan Perera looks to defend but ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads there.
Tossed up ball on off, Lasith Embuldeniya looks to defend but ends up getting it safely to the man at leg slip, off the inner half.
Very full and outside off, Embuldeniya digs it out back on the track.
Floated on off, Lasith defends it to the leg side.
Comes down the track and looks to go big over long on. Ends up mistiming it to the fielder there. A single.
FOUR! That is a boundary. Nicely hit. Full length ball around off, Dilruwan Perera gets down and sweeps it in front of square leg for a boundary.
Flighted outside off, left alone.
BEATEN! Lasith Embuldeniya is lucky he did not get an edge there. Full and outside off, Embuldeniya comes forward and looks to drive but gets beaten on the outside edge there.
Outside off, this time Embuldeniya leaves it alone.
Short length delivery on top of middle, Lasith jumps to play at it but misses and takes it on his body.
Full and outside off, Perera drives it to cover-point who makes a diving stop. Keeps it down to one.
Full and around off, Perera defends it down to mid on.
Short length ball, Dilruwan sits under that one.
On off, Perera clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Floated on middle, defended back on the track.

Slower in the air and on off and middle, Perera pushes it to the right of the bowler and strays outside of his crease. Leach dives to his right, takes the ball and throws it back to the keeper. Perera was slow but eventually gets back.
Sharp turn there. It lands outside off and moves away further. Dilruwan lets that one be.
Flighted again, around off, defended to the off side.
SIX! Oh... that is all the way! Flighted outside off, Dilruwan Perera dances down the track and lofts it well over the head of the man at long off. Perera knew it the moment he hit that.
Lasith Embuldeniya is the next man in.

OUT! TAKEN! One brings two they say. James Anderson gets another wicket. The three changes that Sri Lanka made for this match - all of them register ducks. Tough conditions for fast bowling but not tough for Anderson. Full length delivery, Lakmal comes forward and goes for the drive. He though gets a thick outside edge and it goes over the head of Crawley at gully. He takes a sharp catch.
Short of a length and outside off, defended to the off side.
Suranga Lakmal comes out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Oh dear! Oh dear! Niroshan Dickwella departs. Commentator's curse, given that Arnold was praising him a while ago. And it is yet another five-wicket haul for James Anderson in Tests. His 30th in fact. Well bowled. It was full and outside the off pole area, Niroshan Dickwella wanted to clear the head of mid off there. He strokes his drive uppishly. But it was not aerial enough. Jack Leach, at mid off, runs to his right, stretches his arms and takes a very good catch. For a moment, it looked like it would get away from Leach. But he hangs on. Dickwella falls 8 runs shy of his maiden Test hundred.
Full length ball around the off stump area, Dickwella drives but finds short mid off there.

Shortish length delivery just outside the off pole area, dabbed to the man at cover-point. Niroshan eyeing his first 100 here. He has looked very good so far. Russel Arnold (on air) is very impressed with him.
Full length ball around the off pole, blocked to the off side.
Flighted ball on the middle stump line, defended to the leg side. Better from Leach.

FOUR! The slowness of the track coming to play here. Nicely dealt with by Perera. A touch short, outside the off stump area, Perera goes back and guides it nicely behind square on the off side. A fielder gives chase, but in vain.
Leach gives it a nice loop and bowls it outside the off pole channel, Perera rocks back but lets it be in the end.
Fuller in length ball on the off pole area, blocked back on the pitch.
Flatter and outside the off stump line, Dilruwan drives it to cover.
Niroshan Dickwella has options on the on side. Tossed up around the off stump, ND gets down and paddles it nicely through short fine leg. Takes a single.
Full length and angled in near the off pole line, blocked to the off side.
Short length delivery, Perera sits under that one.
Full length ball around the off pole, Dilruwan comes forward and fends it out.
Outside off, dabbed to the off side.

Dickwella moves into the 90s here! He is very good when playing his shots as well. Full length ball on middle and leg, Niroshan Dickwella clips it through the mid-wicket region. The fielder at deep square leg runs to his right but the Lankans pick up three by the time the throw comes in.
Full length delivery around off, Niroshan is solid as a rock in his defence there. 88 dots in his innings so far.
Tossed up on middle, Perera defends it back to the bowler.
Flatter ball outside off, DP pushes it to cover.
On middle, defended back to the bowler.

A big appeal for caught behind turned down! Floated ball outside off, turning away. Perera looks to defend but seems to have missed. Buttler collects and appeals but the umpire is not interested.  The English players think of a review but they opt against it.
Loopy ball on off, Perera prods forward and then defends it to the off side.
On the pads, Niroshan swats it down to the fine leg region and they cross.
Outside off, left alone by Perera.
Full ball on middle, Dilruwan pushes it back to the bowler.
Good length ball outside off, Perera lets it go to the keeper.
Full ball outside off, Niroshan taps it to the deep point region and crosses over for a single.
Good length ball outside off, Dickwella plays it uppishly to point but luckily for Dickwella, it lands safely in front of the fielder.
Full ball outside off, Dickwella drives it to cover.
Flighted on middle, Dickwella works it to the leg side for a single.
On middle, Perera plays it to long on for a single.

NOT OUT! Pitching outside leg and England lose one of their reviews. Floated ball on the pads, Perera looks to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. Buttler and Leach appeal but the umpire is not confident. Both the keeper and the bowler look confident and they convince Root to take the review. Joe Root takes it. Ultra Edge shows that there is no bat on it while Ball Tracker shows that it is pitching outside leg. Strange review.

Time for a review here! Interesting, it was down the leg side but still, Root, has opted to review that, for a LBW. Dilruwan Perera is the man in question. Let's see if he has got any bat on it whatsoever. Ultra Edge is in... Flat line as the ball passes the bat. Right, in comes Ball Tracker. PITCHING OUTSIDE LEG, nothing further to move on here. On-field decision stays and the tourists lose a review.
Flatter on middle, Dickwella works it to mid-wicket where Bairstow makes a fumble and that allows the batters to pick up a single.
Full ball outside off, Niroshan digs it to cover.
Shorter on the pads, Dickwella plays it to short fine leg.

The Sri Lankan physio is out here. He is giving some assistance to Niroshan. Possibly some cramp. Water and tablets are being given to Dickwella. Right, he is back on his feet and will continue, while the physio makes his way out.
Full ball outside off, Perera shoulders arms to it.
Full ball outside off, Dickwella drives it to deep point for a single. This is now Dickwella's highest score in Test cricket.
Back of a length ball on off, Dickwella taps it to the point region for a dot.
On a length on middle, Dickwella plays it back to the bowler.
Fullish ball on off, Dickwella plays it to point.
FOUR! Nicely guided away! Dickwella moves to the 80s! Good length ball outside off, Dickwella guides it to the backward point region and picks up a boundary.

Will Sam Curran continue from the other end? No, it is James Anderson. Just the pattern that has always been the case for England. He will be looking for a fifer here. He has figures of 23-12-29-4 so far.
Safely negotiated! Tossed up outside off, Perera blocks it to cover. Just a single from the over.
Loopy ball on middle, Perera works it to mid-wicket.
Floated on off, Perera solidly defends it to the off side.
Flighted ball outside off, Perera leaves it alone.
Loopy ball on middle, Perera lunges forward and then defends it to the leg side.
Short ball on middle, Dickwella pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.

We are back for the afternoon session then. Niroshan Dickwella and Dilruwan Perera are out in the middle. So are the English players. Jack Leach will continue with the ball for the English. Here he comes...
... Day 2, Session 2...

Right then, that caps off an excellent session for Sri Lanka. They have done really well so far and with ample time still left in the Test match, they would feel that they are in no hurry. Meanwhile, England need to net a few wickets in the immediate overs after Lunch. If they cannot, the Lankans might well and truly run away with this match. Join us at around 1240 local (0710 GMT) to find out how the post-Lunch session pans out...

Nothing much for the visitors, except the initial success. It was once again their go-to-man, James Anderson, who got the much-needed breakthrough, that of Angelo Mathews. And shortly after that Wood removed Ramesh Mendis, courtesy a splendid catch from Jos Buttler. But after that, the bowlers had to toil hard, with no real success. The spinners were not spared at all, with Perera not afraid of dancing down the track to go for the lofted shots.

The session did not start off on a great note for the Lankans, as they lost their centurion, Mathews, pretty early. The debutant, Ramesh Mendis, soon followed. At 243/6, it looked like the Sri Lankans might at best get to 275 or so. But Dickwella and Perera had other plans. They have stitched a 50-plus partnership and Sri Lanka are well past 300 now.

It is another really good session of tough Test match cricket. England had the honours early on but Sri Lanka have come, roaring back in. This partnership between Dickwella and Perera is 70 and going strong. They have done a terrific job so far.
Full ball on off, Perera defends it back to the bowler. LUNCH ON DAY 2.
Short ball around middle, Perera ducks under it.
Full ball on off, DP drives it to mid off.
Short ball around middle, Dilruwan ducks under it.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Perera works it to mid-wicket.
Short ball on the pads, Dickwella works it down to fine leg for a single.
Niroshan dances down the track and nudges this fuller ball through mid on and crosses for a single.
Flatter ball on middle, clipped to square leg for a quick single. There is an overthrow at the bowler's end but they choose to be happy with the one there.
On off and middle, pushed back to Jack.
This time it is flatter and outside off, Perera stays back to block it. Gets an underedge of sorts and looks to push it away from hitting the stumps. No damage done here, for Sri Lanka.
Flighted ball outside the off pole, Dilruwan taps it to the off side and says no.
Flighted delivery, outside off, driven to cover.

Well, nothing much for the English there. Short ball, Niroshan Dickwella goes for the pull but he misses. Ends up getting hit on the body and the ball goes behind for Jos Buttler. Dickwella survives. Hang on... replays are in. Hmm... there was a bottom edge onto the thigh pad there, as it goes to Buttler on the bounce.
Full length delivery on the middle stump line, Dickwella flicks it to the leg side.
On middle, pulled to deep backward square leg for two.

FOUR! Oh... no chance for Buttler there. It was well and truly away from him. Good energy from Sam Curran as well. He bowls another short delivery, Niroshan Dickwella goes for a pull shot. Gets an edge but gets it well wide of Buttler and gets it down to the fine leg fence.
Short length ball, Niroshan lets it be.

In the air... but it gets away from Crawley, at leg gully. Short length delivery around off, Dickwella goes for a pull shot. Gets a top edge but luckily, gets it over Zak Crawley at leg gully. A couple taken before he runs and cuts it off.
End of another tight over. Outside off, Dilruwan rocks back but ends up leaving it in the end.
JL tosses this outside off, Perera taps it to the off side.
Tossed up, on off and middle, Dilruwan keeps it out.
Tossed up ball on the middle stump line, DP drives but finds cover there. They decide against taking the single.
Tossed up delivery around the off pole, pushed down to long on. They cross.
Looped up on the off pole line, blocked to the leg side. 'Bowled Leachy' says one of the English players.
Full length delivery, angled into middle and leg, Dilruwan Perera taps it to the off side. A tidy over.
Full and angled into the off pole, Perera pushes it back to the bowler.
Another fullish length delivery, Dilruwan is solid in his defence here.
Fullish and around off, blocked to the off side.
Another shortish length ball, on the pads, worked to fine leg, for a run.
Sam comes from 'around the wicket and bangs it in shortish, outside the off pole, tapped to the man at backward point.
Sam Curran is back on. 13-2-45-0 are his figures so far.
Looped up ball on the off stump, blocked.

300 up for the Lankans. Brilliant. Was not even looking possible at one stage but this partnership has made it come by, for the hosts. Jack Leach loops this around the off pole line, pushed down to mid on for one.

Brilliant fielding. Flatter and outside the off pole line, Dilruwan Perera rocks back and cuts it through point. Sibley, who was at cover-point, runs to his left, dives and cuts it out well. Keeps it down to just the single.
Fuller in length ball around the off pole, Dilruwan prods forward and blocks it.
Similar line and length, Perera tries to drop it on the off side again but misses.
Flatter ball outside the off stump area, Dilruwan goes onto his back foot and keeps it out on the off side.
On off, pushed to cover.
Flighted ball on middle, Dickwella plays it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Smashed! Dickwella is playing really well. Tossed up on middle, Dickwella goes down on his knees and then slog sweeps it to the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Short ball on middle, Perera pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
50-run stand comes up! Flighted ball outside off, Dickwella drives it through cover for a single. Excellent stand and it has come in good time as well.
Floated on off, Dickwella pushes it to cover-point.
Flatter ball on middle, Perera plays it back to the bowler.
Up and over! Tossed up outside off, Perera prods forward and then lifts it over the cover fielder. A couple taken before the fielder cuts it off.
Loopy ball on off, Perera prods forward and then blocks it to cover.
Floated ball outside off, Perera leaves it alone.
Slower through the air on middle, Dickwella flicks it to deep square leg and crosses over for the single.
Tossed up on the pads, Dickwella flicks it to mid-wicket.
Quicker on middle, DP nudges it to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball on middle, Perera defends it to short leg.
Floated ball on middle and leg, Perera taps it to leg slip.
Floated on off, Dickwella uses his feet and then drives it to long off for a single.
On off, pushed to cover.

Falls short! Dickwella is really lucky there! Loopy ball on off, Dickwella looks to sweep but it takes the top edge. It lobs in the air towards deep square leg. Leach runs ahead but it lands just ahead of him. Two taken.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Flatter ball outside off, punched to cover.
Floated on off, Perera blocks it to cover.
Flighted on middle, Dickwella dances down the track and then flicks it wide of long on for a single.
Loopy ball on middle, Perera works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Good hit from Dilruwan Perera! Floated ball on middle, Perera dances down the track and then lifts it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
On middle, blocked back to the bowler.
FOUR! Swept and swept well! Beautifully hit from Dickwella! Flighted ball on middle, Dickwella sweeps it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Quicker on the pads, Dilruwan flicks it to square leg where Lawrence misfields and allows the batters to take a single.
Flatter on middle, Perera plays it back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on off, Perera prods forward and then blocks it to the off side.
Flighted ball outside off, Niroshan drives it to deep cover for a single.
A maiden over from Leach. Looped up delivery outside the off pole area, Dilruwan Perera taps it to the off side.
That is the line Jack would look to settle into. More of wicket-to-wicket. He loops this on off and middle, Perera strides forward in defense.
Loopy ball on off and middle, Perera defends it to the off side.
Identical delivery, identical result.
This time it is fuller in length delivery and on the middle stump line, defended to the off side.
Flatter ball outside the off stump line, Dilruwan goes onto the back foot and taps it to the man at short third.
Loopy one on the off stump line, blocked.
Hit that well but straight to the fielder. Flatter delivery on the pads, Perera camps back and pulls it firmly, but finds deep square leg there. Hence, they get just the one.
Lunges forward and keeps this loopy ball out, back on the track.
Flatter off break on the middle stump, Dilruwan flicks but short leg keeps it out.
An armball, flatter and on middle, tucked to mid-wicket and DP exchanges ends with Niroshan.
Lands the off spinner on the middle pole line, Dilruwan Perera goes back and keeps it out to the man at backward square leg.
Shortish and outside off, Perera taps it to the short third man region and takes a single.
Full toss on the off stump line, Dilruwan misses out there. He is only able to tap it down to mid on for a dot. He would be kicking himself for missing to hit that one.
An easy brace here. Outside off, Perera steers it behind square on the off side and comes back in for the second.
Good come back from Jack Leach though. Loopy delivery around the off pole line, defended back on the track.
On off, blocked to the leg side.
FOUR! Oh... he drives him straightaway. Leach floats this on middle and leg, Dilruwan Perera dances down and lofts the drive well over mid on. The ball gets into the fence on a couple of bounces.
Jack Leach is into the attack.
Pushes this fuller in length delivery to the off side and gets to the other end. The conditions are still very good for batting.
Floated on the off pole line, Perera lunges forward and keeps that out.
Floated ball on the middle pole, blocked to the on side.
Flatter delivery outside the off pole, Perera rocks back and cuts it on the off side. Says no to a single.
Floated delivery on off and middle, Dilruwan keeps it out.

FIFTY! Full toss on off, Dickwella nudges it down to mid off for a run. And that will be a half century for Niroshan Dickwella. Yesterday, he played with Mathews. Today, he has to bat well, along with the tail.

Drinks! England have done well in the morning session. They have picked up a couple of wickets, including that of Angelo Mathews. It was Anderson yet again who started it with Wood doing a very good again. Sri Lanka now depend on Niroshan Dickwella to get them to a good score. He has looked good so far and is just one short of fifty. The hosts would want him to continue and not throw it away.

That will be safe. Presence of mind as to where the fielders are. Shortish and around off, Dickwella swings across the line. Hits it uppishly but it falls safely ahead of Curran at fine leg. A single and Dickwella moves to 49 now.

FOUR! Gone fine. No leg slip so no worries for Niroshan Dickwella. Jonny Bairstow was at leg slip a while ago, not now. Niroshan Dickwella uses the angle of this shortish length ball and tickles it down nicely to the fine leg region and gets a boundary.
Shortish length delivery on top of leg, Niroshan Dickwella sits under that one there. Hang on, No Ball called here. It has been called as Wood overstepped.
Shortish and on off, Dickwella clips but finds the man at short mid-wicket there.
Short and on top of the stumps, the Sri Lankan wicket-keeper sits under that one.
Shortish length ball, pulled away in the gap behind square on the leg side. Should be at least two as deep backward square leg runs to his right and mops it up. Yes, two runs it is.
Short length delivery, Niroshan ducks under it.
Full on middle, Dilruwan plays it back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on middle, DP works it to mid-wicket.
Floated ball outside off, Dickwella plays it to deep cover and collects a run.
Flatter ball on middle, Perera nudges it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up ball on middle, Dilruwan defends it back to the bowler.
Bess starts with a flatter ball outside off, Dickwella cuts it through the cover-point region for a single.

This is going to be very interesting. Dom Bess comes back into the attack. 18-1-54-0 are his figures so far. Russel had stated (during the Pitch Report) that the spinners could get into the act today. Let's see how Dom goes about then.
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball on middle, Perera works it to mid-wicket.
Sharp bumper on middle from Wood, Perera does well to duck under it.
Good length ball on off, Perera defends it to mid off.
Fullish ball on off, Dilruwan drives but finds the fielder at mid off.
Back of a length ball on middle, Perera nudges it to mid-wicket.
Full ball on off, Dickwella defends it to the mid off region.
Outside off, left alone.
Good length ball outside off, Dickwella pushes it to cover-point.
Good length ball outside off, Dickwella lets it go to the keeper.

FOUR! Really good shot from Dickwella again! Fullish ball outside off, Dickwella drives it through the covers region. The fielder gives it a chase but in vain as the ball touches the ropes in the end.
Full ball on off, Niroshan looks to flick but gets a leading edge back to mid off. A safe leading edge.
Good length ball on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Good length ball outside off, Dickwella pushes it to the cover-point region and collects a run.
Slower ball on middle, Niroshan works it to the leg side.
Short ball around middle and leg, Dickwella ducks under it.
FOUR! Creamed! Dickwella is looking good so far! Full ball outside off, Dickwella lunges forward and drives it through the covers region for a boundary.
Fullish ball on off, Dickwella pushes it to mid off.
Good length ball outside off, angling in. Perera watches it carefully and then leaves it alone.
Good length ball on off, defended out to the off side.
Full ball on off, Perera pushes it to mid off.
Full delivery outside the off stump line, Perera shoulders arms to it.
Good length ball on off, Perera solidly blocks it to cover.
Good length ball on the pads, Dickwella works it to the square leg region for a single.
Dilruwan Perera is the next man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Down the leg side, it is a brilliant grab. Would you believe that? Would you believe that? Wow! Fullish length ball on the pads, Mendis looks to tickle it down to the fine leg region. Gets an edge on it and the ball goes to the left of Jos Buttler, down the leg side. Buttler dives to that side and takes a very good catch. Wood's introduction on Day 2 works wonders. He gets his second. Mendis goes for a duck on debut. Not the debut, he would have wanted.
Good length and outside off, Niroshan taps it on the off side and takes one.

Good length ball around the off stump, Dickwella pushes it in front of mid on. Initially seems interested for a single. That prompts Ramesh to stray out of his crease. But then, Niroshan Dickwella, later on, says no and sends him back.
Full and on the off pole line, defended to the off side.

FOUR! Good shot. Second boundary of the morning for Dickwella. Full length ball, Niroshan Dickwella pushes it wide of mid on. Just a defensive push it was. The man at mid on backtracks and gives chase but comes second in the race, to the boundary.
Full length delivery, Niroshan pushes it to the man at cover. Follows it up with a 'no' to the non-striker.
Mark Wood is into the attack. 17-2-47-1 are his figures so far.
In the channel outside off, RM leaves that alone.
Short ball around middle, Mendis sits under that one.

Short of a length delivery on the body, Ramesh Mendis offered no shot there. It clips his body and goes behind square on the leg side. They take a single but since Mendis offered no shot there, he has to go back, to the striker's end.
Full and around the off pole, Ramesh defends it out to the off side.
Outside off, left alone.
Full length ball on off, Mendis fends it out solidly. First ball in Test cricket negotiated out safely.

FOUR! That is a boundary for Dickwella. The second one in his innings. Spoils Curran's over somewhat. Short length delivery outside the off pole zone, Niroshan Dickwella stands tall and cuts it through the backward point region.
Full length delivery outside the off stump area, the left-hander defends it out.
Full and on middle, ND clips it through the square leg region and takes a couple.
Full delivery, Niroshan Dickwella defends it to the man at short mid-wicket.
Full and swinging down the leg side, Niroshan misses his flick.
Full length ball, Dickwella turns it to the leg side for a dot.
Ramesh Mendis, the debutant, is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Hmm... we got there in the end. It is a superb review from England. They knew that they needed to get rid of Mathews. Full length ball on off and middle, Angelo Mathews looks to defend that but to the naked eye he seems to have missed it. The ball hits the pads and goes to Buttler, who takes it. England go up in appeal for a caught behind but the umpire is unmoved. Joe Root decides to take the review though. The ball is very close to the bat and the third umpire calls for the Ultra Edge. Right then, what do we have there? There is a spike as the ball passes the bat. Out it will be. Yes, but there is some confusion and long delay from the third umpire. Finally, he is satisfied and asks the on-field umpire to reverse his decision. Phew.... it took ages to convey the decision. Superb piece of bowling from Anderson. He got that to jag off the seam. End of a brilliant knock from Angelo Mathews. But his wicket has given an opening to England early on Day 2.

England have taken a review! Angelo Mathews is the man in question. The Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that there is a spike as the ball passed the bat. The third umpire first tells the on-field umpire to stay with the original decision but then realizes that the catch has been taken and the decision is reversed.
Full length ball, Angelo Mathews pushes it to the left of mid on but the fielder dives in that direction and keeps it out. Anderson reckons he was a bit fuller there.
Fullish length delivery, seaming in a little, around the off pole area, Mathews is solid in his defence.
Full ball on middle, Angelo defends it out.
Good length delivery outside the off stump line, AM lets it be.

An appeal for a LBW but not given. It was too high. Good length delivery around off and middle, Mathews looks to play at that but misses. Gets hit on the top of his pads. Anderson and England appeal but to no avail.
James Anderson will bowl from the other end.
Length ball around the off stump line, fended out back on the pitch.
Length delivery around the off stump, Niroshan stands tall and defends it out.

First runs of the day. Full length delivery, Angelo Mathews drives it through the cover-point region. The fielder gives chase and dives near the boundary. To the naked eye, he seems to have done well but the umpires want to have a look. It is taken upstairs and replays are in. The umpires are satisfied with the save. Just the 3 runs then.
Full and around the off pole line, Angelo Mathews defends that to the cover region.
Full length ball around the off pole, Angelo fends it out.
Full length delivery around off, Mathews defends it to the off side.
We are all set to begin Day 2! The England players make their way out to the field, followed by Angelo Mathews and Niroshan Dickwella. Sam Curran will start with the ball for the visitors.

James Anderson has his thoughts to share about Day 1. Says that he was delighted with the way he bowled and was happy with his rhythm. States that when one comes to Sri Lanka, one does not expect to bowl well, but he is happy with himself. Adds that it was a tiring Day 1 but says that it is important now to put that behind and move on now. Says that they need to keep bowling in the right areas now. States that the bowlers bowled good lengths with the new ball on Day 1. Reckons it will be pretty much the same on Day 2 as well.

Pitch Report- Russel Arnold is out in the middle for the Pitch Report. He says that the pitch will start to deteriorate from now on and says that there are early signs of it. Reckons that the spinners will slowly start having an impact on the game now. Feels that Sri Lanka should allow the pitch to wear down more.

England, on the other hand, toiled very hard in the field. They kept the run rate in check but the problem is that they have not been able to take as many wickets as they would have liked. James Anderson was the star with the ball as he picked up 3 wickets out of the 4 to fall but credit must also be given to Mark Wood for bowling a fine, fine spell. The spinners did not look threatening. They will hope that they can pick up a few quick wickets and put the hosts on the back foot.

So what happened on Day 1? Sri Lanka did not have a good start as they lost two wickets quickly but Angelo Mathews stitched partnerships with Thirimanne first and then with Chandimal to ensure that they end the day on top. Mathews scored a fine ton and is still going strong in the middle while Chandimal perished after scoring a 50. They are in a very good position and would hope that they can post a challenging first innings total.

Hello and a warm welcome to the second day's play of the second Test match between England and Sri Lanka. Day 1 belonged to the hosts but England are not out of it yet as they know one or two quick wickets will bring them back in the game. Their bowlers have tried very hard but that has not borne fruit as yet and they will look to make a comeback. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, would want to keep churning out the runs.
... Day 2, Morning Session ...

Right then, Sri Lanka would definitely be the happier side at the end of Day 1 but they will have to come out and do it again on Day 2. They will be hoping to bat long and end their first innings on a high. England, on the other hand, would be hoping for some success in the morning as they aim to wrap up the Sri Lankan batting quickly. Do join us for Day 2 on Saturday, 23rd January 2021 at 1000 local (0430 GMT) for all the action. Until then, cheers!

Angelo Mathews starts off by saying that the openers got out early and they had to see through the early phase and wait for the ball to get slightly older. Praises the bowlers of England for their work. Feels that he got into a good rhythm in the last innings in the first Test but he had to work extremely hard as the English bowlers gave nothing away. Shares that life is not easy in the bubble but playing at the same venue helps in knowing the conditions better. Feels that if the weather remains this hot and humid, then the turf will help the spinners and there will be some more turn in the coming days. States that they just want to get as many runs as possible in the first innings and cannot afford to relax.

The star of the day with the bat has to be Angelo Mathews! He looked in control right from the beginning even though he walked in with Sri Lanka in a spot of bother. Mathews brought all his experience into play and batted with good intent. He will be thrilled to get his maiden Test ton in Galle and would look to make it a daddy hundred. Here he comes to have a quick chat...

England tried their best but it was a toil for them. Hot and humid conditions along with an unresponsive surface - The Three Lions braved everything but managed to pick only four wickets. The spinners didn't get much purchase and apart from one Jack Leach's ball which gripped and turned, there wasn't anything threatening. The bowler of the day has to be James Anderson for his three wickets but you need to applaud Mark Wood for his hostile spells.

End of an absorbing day of Test cricket! Sri Lanka will be very pleased with their efforts after winning the toss. It though started on a sorry note, Angelo Mathews' partnerships with Lahiru Thirimanne and Dinesh Chandimal made sure that the hosts kept a strong grip on the proceedings.
Hurls in a length ball in the zone outside off, Dickwella shoulders arms. End of the over and that will be STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Slants in a fuller length ball around off, Dickwella presses forward and pushes it towards mid on.
FOUR! Easy runs! Anderson errs in his line on this occasion and bowls it too straight. Fullish and angling down the leg side, Dickwella nudges it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Pitches it up and around off, Dickwella produces a copybook forward defensive shot.
Anderson gets closer to the off stump, angling in, Dickwella defends it from the back foot to the off side.
Good length delivery outside off going straight on after landing, nicely left alone by Dickwella.
Shows the full face of the bat, does Angelo. Does well to show his solid defense. Sri Lanka would just want to go through these last few moments unscathed.
Drives this one to the cover region. No runs as this one was straight to the fielder.
On a length and outside off, Mathews looks to slash this one away but this one comes off the inner half of the willow and goes to the cover region.
Short of a length and around off, Mathews jumps and is able to block this one nicely.
Slightly fuller and on the pads, Mathews clips this one nicely through square leg. Bess, from fine leg, runs to his left and keeps this one down to just a couple.
Length and around off, Mathews keeps this one out towards the cover region.
Better this time from the batsman, presents a straight bat to a full delivery and defends it back.
A bit of a mishit! Anderson serves it full and close to off, stopping a bit onto the batsman, Dickwella is early into the shot and pushes it aerially towards mid off. Doesn't carry.
Jimmy goes fuller and close to off, Dickwella allows the ball to come to him and then blocks it near his front pad.
On a good length and close to off, Dickwella stays back and taps it down to covers.
Slightly short this time, around off, Niroshan gets back and plays it down with an angled bat to point.
A confident push. Anderson plants a fuller length ball on off, Dickwella pushes it from the middle of his bat to covers.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Angelo looks to tuck this one away to the leg side but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards the cover region.
On the pads, clipped through the mid-wicket region for a quick run. The call was quick and the response was good to complete the run with ease.
It has turned a bit gloomy with dark clouds hanging above the stadium. Expect the umpires to keep an eye on the light meter.
Pitched up and around off, Niroshan worked this one towards the mid off fielder.
Good length delivery around that fourth stump channel, Dickwella punches but finds the fielder at covers.
Again, shows the full face of the blade and fends this one back towards the younger Curran.
Length and around off, Dickwella is solid in keeping this one out.

FOUR! Finds the gap and the timing is superb! Fuller in length around middle and leg, Mathews picks it off his pads and flicks it through square leg. It runs through a sea of crows and finds the fence.
Switches to over the wicket for Mathews. Delivers a full ball on off and the batsman works it wristily to mid on.
Sliding down the leg side, Dickwella fails to flick and it goes off his pads to fine leg for a leg bye.
Shortish and close to off, Niroshan goes on his toes and taps it down to covers.
Too full on this occasion, Dickwella plays the on drive but finds the mid on fielder.
Anderson speeds in from 'round the wicket for the left-hander and angles in a full length ball on off, Dickwella defends it back.
Short of a length and around the off pole, Angelo is up to the task and fends this one out well.
A single this time. On a good length and outside off, Dickwella pushes this one to the cover region and the fielder there fumbles slightly and so the batters are able to complete the run.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Slightly shorter and outside off, slashed away, but straight to the point fielder.
Pulls his length back and delivers it on off, Dickwella is on the back foot as he defends.

Lovely shot, through extra cover. Curran thrives for some movement and in that greed, he overpitches it around off, Dickwella drives it and Anderson gives the chase. He pulls it back near the fence and they take only two. Poor running, the pair thought that Jimmy won't be chasing it down.
Good length ball on off, Angelo defends it off his back foot to complete the first over with the second new ball.
Sam Curran to bowl from the other end. 8-2-30-0 are his numbers so far.
Here it comes... Right there! A big inswinger from Jimmy, fullish and on off, curling back into the batsman, Mathews is up to the task and plays it out from the inner half to mid on.
Yet another delivery in the corridor outside off, Mathews is happy leaving those. Away, away, away... is Anderson planning for a big inswinger?
Anderson hurls across a fuller length ball outside off, angling in and once again moving away slightly, Mathews makes a watchful leave.
A length ball this time around off, Mathews goes on the back foot and defends it down on the pitch.
Starts his new spell with a fuller length ball close to off, a hint of away shape, Mathews plays it nice and late as he keeps it out safely to covers.
England have the option to opt for the second new ball and they have taken it immediately. Not surprisingly, James Anderson returns to make the first use of it.
Loopy and on middle, Dickwella does well to keep this one out.
Sweep is out again. It is on middle, Floated delivery. Dickwella sweeps again to fine leg. Picks up a couple.
Loopy and around off, Mathews whips this one through mid-wicket and collects a single.
On middle, clipped to the mid-wicket region.
Floated on middle, Dickwella sweeps this one fine to the short fine leg region. Gets a single.
The reserve umpire is ready with the second new ball. He also has the light meter in his hand. Just 5 more balls to go...
Flighted on off, kept out by ND.
On the pads, helped to the on side for a single. End of another over from Wood in this extended spell, most probably his last of the day.
Slowish yorker around off, Wood wanted to take Dickwella by surprise. Niroshan though digs this one out towards the mid on region. Wood has a cheeky smile on his face, after the delivery.
Length and around off, kept out.
Short length delivery around off, Dickwella sways away, maybe thinks about the ramp shot. Then, thinks slightly better and just lets this through to the keeper.
Short and around off, dabbed to point.
Bumper on middle, Dickwella knows what he has to do. Sits under this one.
On off, pushed to mid on. Just 2 more overs for the second new ball.
Loopy on off, AM works this to covers.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Floated on off, pushed to the off side for a single.
On off, kept out.

HUNDRED FOR ANGELO MATHEWS! A very good knock and he has deservedly reached his century. His 11th in Test cricket and this is his 3rd against the English Lions. Also, if you believe it or not, his FIRST CENTURY in Galle. A job well done, so far. He came in when things were tough but he has done well to stick around and reach his century. Short and around off, Mathews punches this one to the cover region and the batters scamper through for a single.
Back of a length delivery this time around off, Niroshan pushes this one towards mid off.
On off, tapped to covers. 'No' says Dickwella, to his partner.

PLAY AND A MISS! Ohhhh...so close! Wood comes 'round the wicket and bowls a good length delivery around off, Dickwella looks to have a tentative poke away from his body but he misses the ball completely.
Good length and on middle, Mathews clips this one to fine leg. Picks up a single. 99 now. One more away from getting his century. This now is Angelo's highest Test score in Galle.
Length delivery outside off, tails in slightly after pitching, Mathews pushes this one to the left of mid on.
Down the leg side, on a good length, Angelo looks for the tuck away but then decides to just leave it alone at the last moment.
Flatter and outside off, Angelo waits for it and then slams this one through cover-point. Takes a single and will retain the strike for the next over. Is on 98 now.
Skips down the track and works this to the right of mid off for a single.
Short and outside off, Mathews punches this one to deep point. One more run. Moves onto 97 now.
Loopy and lands it around the off pole, AM taps it towards point. Looks for the single but is sent back by Niroshan.
Tossed up and around off, Dickwella whips this one towards mid on. Gets to the other end safely.
Shorter in length and around off, Angelo backs away and punches this one to the cover-point region. Crosses over for a single.
Pushed to the cover-point region. Just 2 off the over.
Shortish and around off, Dickwella punches this one to the point region.
On off, played to point. No is the call, for the single.
200 up for Sri Lanka! Back of a length and on middle, Niroshan hops and tucks this one to the fine leg region. Curran does well in the deep to dive and keep this one out. Saves a couple of runs.
Gets his bat down in time to defend this one solidly.
Short and wide outside off, Dickwella cuts this one but it comes off the under-edge and it goes to the point region.
On middle, kept out safely again. Only 6 more overs until the second new ball is available.
Flighted and around off, Angelo keeps this one out.
Shortish around off, pushed to covers.

A bit of a funny moment between the overs! One of the umpires wanted his sunglasses and signalled for it. The English players near the boundary line thought that he has called for drinks. They went in only to be sent back.
Short and around off, Angelo plays this to the fielder at short cover.
Comes on his front foot and blocks this one out.
Flighted around off, pushed to the cover region.
Only 2 runs off the over. Good length around off, Niroshan pushes this one towards the cover region. Looks for the single but is quick to deny it as well.
Around off, on a length, Niroshan works this one to the cover-point region this time.
Length and around off, Dickwella pushes this one to point.
Back of a length and around off, well kept out towards the cover region.
Short and around off, Mathews hooks this one to the leg side. Gives the strike back to Niroshan.

EDGY. Fuller and outside off, Dickwella looks to drive this one but the ball takes the inside edge, goes past the leg pole, to the square leg region for a single. Wood would be disappointed as he would have wanted to get a couple of chances at Dickwella.
Dickwella is off the mark. Floated on middle, tucked to deep square leg for a single.
On middle, blocked off the front foot. Leach getting some purchase off this surface. Can he make the most of it?
Tossed up and around off, Niroshan skips down the track and pushes this one back to the bowler.
Floated around off, pushed to covers.
Flighted and around off, Dickwella keeps it out.
Floated on middle, tucked to mid-wicket.
Too full in length around off, Mathews tries to drive but it takes the inner half and rolls to short mid-wicket.
Slips another length ball down the leg side, Mathews tries to flick but misses.
Bouncer, the batsman ducks under that one.
Bowls it from wide of the crease, Mathews stands back and defends it down to mid-wicket.
Good length delivery going down the leg side, Mathews shoulders arms to allow it through.
Angling down the leg side, a length ball, Mathews lets it be.
Quicker one but too straight and Mathews works it through mid-wicket for three runs.
Gets forward to a full ball and defends it solidly.
Flatter and fuller on middle, it's pushed back to the bowler.
That is defended solidly off the front foot. It's important for England that Leach ties up one end.
Full and floated on off, Mathews is forward as he blocks it to the off side.
Flighted and outside off, Mathews allows it through to the keeper.

DRINKS. A wicket at the right stage for the visitors. Angelo and Chandimal were just motoring along but Wood came and he has broken this century stand. Now, they see that the door is slightly ajar and would look to make the most of it. If they are able to scalp a couple more wickets before Stumps on Day 1, then they will go back as the happier team. Sri Lanka have done well so far and now they will want to see off the final stretch of play without any casualties. Also, Niroshan Dickwella is the new batter in for the hosts.

OUT! It's cannoning into the leg stump and the century partnership is broken. Big smile on Joe Root's face. Hard work pays off for Wood. He might not be too accurate in this spell but he has worked hard and deserves this breakthrough. Hurls across a length ball around off and it jags into the batsman with the angle, Chandimal is caught on the back foot in an attempt to defend it. He misses and is trapped on the pads. The appeal is made and the umpire agrees. Chandimal reviews the decision but it's all red in the Ball Tracker. Chandimal returns and Wood thanks the heavens. First wicket for him in this series.
Shortish and on middle, the batsman jumps and fends it off on the off side. It's in the gap and they cross for a run.

Sri Lanka review! Dinesh Chandimal is the man in question. He has been given out for LBW by the on-field umpire and he wants this checked upstairs. Ultra Edge rolls in and it confirms that there is not bat involved there. Ball Tracker rolls in and.... THREE REDS. Will remain out.
Angling down the leg side, Angelo fails to flick and it clips his pads on its way to fine leg for a leg bye. Hang on, the umpire has given it as a dead ball. Wasn't Mathews offering any shot?
A length ball on middle, worked off the pads the leg side but straight to square leg. Again some confusion over a run but they decided not to take the risk.
Yet another poor delivery. Wood has not looked too effective in this spell. One more ball drifting down the leg side, Mathews makes a leave.
A length ball sliding down the leg side, Mathews tries to flick but misses.
Tossed up ball on middle, worked on the leg side but straight to the fielder.
This time the batter goes back and punches it from the crease for a run on the off side.

Miscommunication. Chandimal dances down the track ad pushes it to mid on. He is halfway down the track eyeing a run but Mathews sends him back. Now, the fielder misfields there, it's Anderson and the batsmen cross.
Uses his feet to come down the track and then pushes it with the spin to covers.
Gives it a good toss and lands it around off, Chandimal defends it from the crease.
Fullish and on off, Chandimal leans forward and pushes it to covers.
A length ball on off, Mathews covers the line and pushes it towards mid on. Screams out a loud no.
Wood has been a bit wayward in this over. Shortish and on middle, Mathews gets inside the line and eases his pull down to deep backward square leg for a couple.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Mathews sticks back and drives it on the up to the cover fielder.
A slower one from the speed merchant, the line remains straight and Mathews sits back to work it towards mid-wicket for a couple.
Good length ball around off, it's defended off the back foot by Mathews.
FOUR! Eased away! A full toss on the pads, Mathews has no qualms in deflecting it neatly to the fine leg fence.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, Chandimal meets it with a dead straight blade.
Full and flighted on off, Chandimal defends it back quietly.
Yet another off drive from the bat of Chandimal and the short cover fielder dives to his right to make the stop.
Tossed up ball landing full on off, Chandimal drives it to short cover.
Flighted and full on middle, Chandimal defends it by getting half-forward.
20th Test fifty for Chandimal! Short in length and outside off, Chandimal stays back and cuts it through point for a couple of runs. Good knock!
Wood serves a good length ball on off, slanting in, Mathews stays back and defensively pushes it out to mid-wicket.
Gets behind the line of a length delivery around off and defends it watchfully.
Shortish and on off, Chandimal gets the chance to move back and manoeuvre it through square leg for a run.
The line is close to off, on a length and angling in, Chandimal offers a dead bat in defense.
Back of a length ball around off, Chandimal stands back and closes the face of his bat to help it towards square leg.
Begins his new spell by spearing in a full ball on off, Chandimal keeps it out safely to mid on.
Mark Wood is back into the attack now. 9-1-31-0 are his numbers so far. Can he inspire his side and break this stand?

An appeal for caught behind but turned down by the umpire. Flatter and around off, Mathews goes on his back foot and looks to punch this one away but misses and the ball spins away and goes to Buttler. A stifled appeal but no says the umpire. They think about the review but decide not to, in the end.
On middle, worked to the leg side for one.
Flatter and around off, AM punches this one to covers for one.
On off, blocked.

100 PARTNERSHIP UP BETWEEN THESE TWO! It has been a very good stand by these two so far and they will want to ensure that they can continue this. They have troubled the bowling of the English Lions and they do not want to stop. Flatter and around off, Mathews punches this one through the cover region and Bess in the deep does well to dive and keep this down to just a couple.
Full on middle, kept out.

Misfield and a single. Wood is the culprit here. Another good length delivery around off, Mathews drives this one to the left of mid off. Wood dives, but only manages to push it behind him. By the time he can cover-up, the batters cross ends.
Good length, outside off, Angelo dabs this one towards cover-point.
Good length and on middle and leg, Mathews looks to clip this one away but he misses and the ball takes the pad and goes to the left of Buttler, who does well to stop this one.
Length and around off again, Mathews pushes this one towards mid on.
On a length and down the leg side, Angelo misses his tuck away.
Around off, length delivery, pushed to the leg side.
On off, well kept out.

BEATEN! Some turn this time around for Leach. Flighted around off, spins away sharply after hitting the deck as the ball misses Chandimal's defensive stroke and goes to Buttler. Some puff of dust also coming out, encouraging signs for the spinners.
Loopy on leg, tucked to the square leg region for a single.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Slightly short and around off, spins away, Angelo waits for it and then guides this one towards backward point. Wood is the fielder there who does well to stop this one. A single taken.
Floated on off, blocked.
Jack Leach is back on now. 13-2-46-0 are his numbers so far.
On off, kept out by Chandimal.
Back of a length and around off, Dinesh works this one to square leg. Comes a few paces ahead looking for the single but he goes back into his crease as he realizes that this will not be possible.
Short of a length and around the off pole, DC hops and fends this one towards the mid off region.
Chandimal comes on his front foot. Blocks it solidly towards covers.
Slightly behind the good length and around off, Dinesh is solid in his defense.
On a good length and around off, pushed to point.
FOUR! A good way to end the over for Sri Lanka and Mathews! Loops it up nicely and lands it around off, Mathews punches this one through covers. It runs away to the ropes.
Flighted around off, Chandimal pushes this one to the cover region for a single.
On middle, blocked to the leg side.

Loopy around off, Chandimal skips down the track and powers this one to the right of the mid off fielder, who does well to dive and half stop this one. The ball goes towards long off and Anderson runs to his left and cleans up. Two runs.
On off, pushed back to Bess.
Dinesh offered a front foot defense to this looped up delivery around off.
Slight movement noticed. Length and around off, nips back in ever-so-slightly as Angelo tucks this one to the leg side. Another maiden for Jimmy.
Outside off, Angelo lets this one through to Buttler.
Pushed with a straight bat towards the left of the mid on fielder.
Well fielded by Lawrence. Good length and outside off, Angelo slaps this one towards the cover region, but Lawrence there, does well to stop this one.
Outside off this time, but on a good length, Angelo plays this one towards mid off this time.
Good length and around off, Mathews pushes this one to the cover region.
Change of ends for James Anderson.
Flatter and around off and middle, AM tucks this one to mid-wicket. Crosses over with a single. 3 runs to start off Bess' new spell.
Comes on his front foot this time and blocks it out.
Floated down the leg side, Angelo just watches this one go to the keeper.
Goes on his back foot and plays this to mid-wicket, to the fielder present there.
Slightly shorter and on middle, Chandimal backs away and works this through mid-wicket. A single.
Floats it up around middle, nudged to square leg for a single.
Dom Bess (15-1-40-0) is back on. Spin from both ends now.
On off, DC blocks.
Shortish and around off, Dinesh backs away and plays this towards covers. They think about the single but the ball is too close for them to attempt this. Do not go for it.
Flat, around off, cut away to point for one.

FOUR! A slightly risky stroke but Mathews made clean contact and he fetches a boundary for himself. Flighted and around off, he steps out of his crease and lofts this one over the mid on region and the ball goes past the ropes for a boundary.
Short and around off, Angelo punches this one to the cover region.
Flighted around off, Mathews works this with soft hands towards short cover.
A dot to end. Another good length delivery around off, Chandimal keeps this one out towards the leg side.
Length and around off, Angelo taps this one towards point. The batters cross ends with a single.
Outside off, Mathews will leave this one in his sleep. And he does the same while he is awake.
Prods forward and blocks this one out with a solid, straight bat.
Similar delivery as the last ball, Mathews offers a similar shot this time around. Which is basically no shot.
On a good length outside off, Mathews does not fall for the temptation to drive. Just leaves it.
Extra loop on this one, full and on off, Chandimal drives but picks out the extra cover fielder.
Flatter and a touch short on off, Chandimal goes back and offers a straight bat in defense.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it watchfully.
Leach drops it short and outside off, Mathews slaps it to deep cover-point for one.
Fuller and on off, Chandimal eases it in the gap at covers for a quick run.
Floated and full around off, Chandimal is on the front foot as he pushes it to covers.
Jack Leach to continue from the opposite end.
Takes a stride forward to a length ball and defends it solidly.
Dark clouds are slowly gathering over the stadium. There is a forecast for rain in the last session and let's pray it stays away.
Fullish and on off, Mathews pushes it off his front foot to mid on.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Angling into the batsman, on a length around middle, Mathews defends it on the leg side.
On a length and outside off, Angelo has nothing to do with it.
Starts with a fuller length ball around off, Mathews is on the front foot as he blocks it to Anderson.

We're back for the evening session. The men concerned are out in the centre. The over-rate has been poor and as a result, we have another 37 overs left in the day's play. James Anderson to begin proceedings. A change of ends for him. Here we go...
.....DAY 1, THIRD SESSION .....

A good session for Sri Lanka! Once again they started on a sorry note by losing an early wicket but since then, Angelo Mathews and Dinesh Chandimal have formed a strong alliance. Apart from Mark Wood's hostile spell, the current pair looked largely untroubled. The English spinners have been very ineffective on an unresponsive track and they need to find a way to bowl with more control. Do join us at 1500 local (0930 GMT) for the last session.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, Chandimal leans forward in defense. That will be TEA ON DAY 1!
Shortish and outside off, Angelo moves back and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Too full and on middle, it's eased down to mid on.
Flatter and on shorter on off, Mathews punches but finds the cover fielder.
Fullish and on middle, Mathews lunges and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it back to the bowler.
Quicker one aroud leg, it's defended from the crease to the leg side.
Helps it with the spin on the leg side but fails to find the gap.
Too full and around leg, Angelo whips it to deep mid-wicket and takes a single.
Tossed up ball on off, Mathes flicks it but finds mid-wicket.
Loopy and full around off, Chandimal is on the front foot as he pushes it with soft hands to covers for one.
Fires a quicker one on middle, Mathews knocks it down through mid on for a run.
Leach flights this one around off, on a fuller length, Chandimal defends it back.
Too full and on off, Mathews drives this time and brings long off into play as he crosses.
A nice loopy full ball around off, Chandimal eases down the track and drives it to long off for a run.
Arm ball on middle, worked with the angle to mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller and on middle, driven down to long off for a run.
Hangs on the back foot and punches it to deep cover for a run.
A full toss on middle, it's knocked down to long on for a run.
Another flick shot but Mathews finds the mid-wicket fielder again.
A full toss on middle, helped on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Punched with sweet timing but not finding the gap at mid on.
Flighted and on middle, worked on the leg side but straight to square leg.
Presses forward and defends it watchfully.
Skidding down the leg side, Chandimal flicks it off the inner half to short fine leg.
Helps it to the right of mid-wicket for an easy run.
Quicker one on off, forced to mid off where the fielder made a good stop.
Full and around off, Chandimal drives it with the spin past covers for a run.
Takes a big stride forward and deends it back to the bowler.
Once again Chandimal comes down the track and this time he pushes it down to long on for one.
Uses his feet and defends it back to the bowler.
Shortish and worked with ease to mid-wicket for a run.
Fullish and around middle, knocked down to long on for a run.
Shortish on middle, worked in the gap at mid-wicket for one.
Flatter on the pads, helped to square leg for a single.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to the left of the bowler who makes a stop.
Gets forward to a full all and defends it soundly.
Tossed up ball on middle, driven back and Leach dived to his left to make the stop.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Lunges to a full ball outside off and pushes it to covers.
Full and flighted on off, defended back to the bowler off his front foot.
Full and flighted outside off, DC is on the front foot again in defense.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it back to the bowler.
Played towards mid-wicket for a single.
Plays it with the spin to the leg side, finds square leg.
Tossed up ball on middle, defended to square leg.
Flighted and on leg, Mathews works it on the leg side but finds short mid-wicket.
Magic spray is out. Chandimal was hit on the gloves in the previous over and he is receiving some treatment.
A length ball around off, Chandimal tucks it behind square leg for two. That should be it for Wood in this spell.
Short again but this time the line is wide outside off, Chandimal slaps it to deep point for a couple of runs.
In all sorts of trouble! A vicious short ball again, on middle and jumping onto the batsman, Chandimal hops and fends it off. It takes his gloves and dies down away from short leg.
A bouncer on middle and leg, Chandimal immediately ducks.
In the gap! Full and on middle, Chandimal flicks it with good timing through mid-wicket for a brace.
Aims for an inswinging yorker but ends up serving a low full toss on off, Chandimal pushes it off the inside half to short mid-wicket. Wood is on the ground after delivering the ball.
Goes on the back foot and works it on the leg side, not in the gap.
Tight run! Loopy delivery around off, Chandimal takes it on the full and eases it towards mid off. He attempts for a quick run and makes it with a dive as Curran misses his shy at the bowler's end.
A touch short and around off, Chandimal punches it from the back foot to mid off.

SIX! This one has gone all the way! Bess gives it a good toss and lands it full around off, Chandimal dances down the track and goes bang down the ground. It goes flying and clears long off. The 50-run stand comes up between the two!
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out to the off side.
Turning down the leg side, Mathews helps it through square leg for a run.

A short delivery is followed up by a 148 kph fuller one, Chandimal brings his bat down as he tries to keep it out. It goes and appears to be going on the full to the square leg fielder who collects and they appeal. The umpires come together and take it upstairs. It's a BUMP BALL.
Wood is really cranking it up. Short and around off at 90 mph, Chandimal ducks at the last moment.
Misses! Beaten for pace. Wood spears in a very full ball on middle and leg, 90 mph, Chandimal tries to flick but misses. Maybe, some inside edge too.
Short delivery again, around off, Mathews gets hold of the pull shot this time and sends it to deep square leg for a run.

LUCKY FOUR! It's gloved. Hostile bowling. Fast and furious. Short and angling down the leg side, Mathews gloves his attempted pull shot wide of the keeper and to the fine leg fence. Fifty up for Angelo, a very good knock by him yet again!
Shortish and on off, Mathews pulls it behind square leg and Sibley makes a fine stop near the rope. Two runs taken.
A bit of drift for Bess as he lands a full ball on off, Chandimal drives it to covers where a fielder intercepts.
Loopy and full outside off, Chandimal presses forward, has a look and then makes a leave.
Some turn on this occasion, around middle and leg, Chandimal walks down the track and helps it in front of square leg.
Fuller and outside off, it's driven through covers for a single.
Goes on the back foot and works it on the leg side, finds the fielder at square leg.
Full and flighted on off, Mathews knocks it across the line and the short mid-wicket fielder dives to make the half-stop. He parries it towards the bowler.
Targets the off stump with a good length ball, Chandimal stays on his toes in defense. Good hostile over by Wood.
Angles in a length ball on off, Chandimal gets right behind the line and defends to the off side.
Physio is out to conduct the mandatory concussion check. Dinesh Chandimal is moving well and is looking fine. Change of helmet for him.

That's a snorter from Mark Wood! Fast and nasty, targeting the head of the batsman. Chandimal takes his eyes off the ball, tries to evade but it pings the grille of his helmet and balloons to Root at wide first slip. The skipper collects and appeals, nothing from the umpire.
Wood overcorrects his line as he spears a full ball on middle and leg, a bit of reverse again but Chandimal flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Oh, that's fabulous! A high class shot by Chandimal. He leans into the fuller length delivery and creams his drive through covers.
Good length ball on middle and leg, it's worked down to fine leg for a run.
Flatter and a bit shorter on off, Mathews gets the time to move back and work it in front of square leg for a run.
A straight bat defensive shot this time by Mathews as he lunges to a full ball on middle.
Add one more delivery to the tally as Mathews is forward and helps it gently to short mid-wicket.
Once again Mathews is very much content in playing out the full deliveries with the spin to short mid-wicket.
Leans forward to a full ball outside off and works it with the spin to short mid-wicket.
Full and floated on middle, Mathews defends it off his front foot to the leg side.

Drinks break. 32 runs in the first hour after Lunch for a loss of one wicket. England started well again with Anderson dismissing Thirimanne immediately but once again Sri Lanka are recovering through the current stand. The pitch is not offering much but Mark Wood got it to reverse in his last over. That might change things around for England. Let's see how the second hour pans out.
Goes fuller and serves it on off, 147 kph, Chandimal drives it back to the bowler.
Shortish and close to off, 140 kph, Chandimal is on his toes in defense.
Good length ball on off, 141 kph, defended off the back foot.

Two noises there as the bowler puts in a stifled appeal for an lbw. Is there some reverse happening for Wood? He hurls in 152 kph full delivery on middle and leg, spearing down as Chandimal fails to flick.
Excellent short delivery, on middle and leg, Chandimal tries to tuck it around the corner but it takes the leading edge and goes safely to covers.
A length delivery outside off, it's left alone by Angelo.

FOUR! Too full in length outside off, Mathews drives it square of the wicket on the off side. The fielder gives the chase from the cover region and slides near the fence to pull it back. The onfield umpire checks upstairs and finds that it's not cleanly done. A boundary signalled.
Flatter and shorter around off, Mathews forces it back to the bowler off his back foot.
Quicker and on middle at 88 kph, it's hit past short leg to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Flatter and on off, Chandimal punches it from the back foot to the right of the bowler.
Flatter and on off, this time the choice of the defensive shot by Dinesh is off the back foot.
Flighted delivery around off, defended off the front foot by Chandimal.
Extra bounce this time, hurrying up the batsman. Back of a length ball around off, Mathews jumps to work it but gets a soft leading edge towards short cover.
On a good length and just outside off, Mathews defends it from the back foot towards mid off.
