Use of the wrists by Chandimal as he works a fuller length ball in front of square leg for a single.
Bouncer around off, Chandimal leans back and sways away from the line of fire.
Spears in a very full ball on middle, some movement in the air at 143 kph, Angelo leans across and flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Wrong line! Wood steams in but slips a length ball down the leg side, Mathews tries to flick but misses.
Change at both ends now. Mark Wood is unleashed into the attack. 0/10 in his 4 overs so far.
Flighted and full on middle, Chandimal defends it off is front foot to short mid-wicket.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Floated one, landing full around of, Dinesh defends it watchfully by pressing forward.
This one is slightly quicker and fuller on middle, Chandimal defends it by getting forward.
Loopy and full on off, slower in pace, Chandimal is on the front foot in defense.
Flatter and a touch shorter on middle, Chandimal goes back and punches it towards mid on.
Dom Bess is back into the attack for his third spell. 0/15 in his 6 overs so far.
In the corridor of uncertainty, the batsman is not interested in playing at that.

FOUR! Squeezes that through! 100 up for Sri Lanka. Fuller length ball around off, Mathews tries to play the cover drive but it takes the outer half of his bat and runs through backward point for a boundary.
This time it's served on a driving length outside off, Mathews makes one more leave.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Mathews waits patiently and then makes a leave.
Back to the channel outside off, on a good length, Mathews lets it be.

FOUR! Nice shot! A very tiny gap between two catching fielders at short mid-wicket but Mathews has found it with surgical precision. Fuller in length on middle, Angelo flicks and shows his class there. Timing and placement. Top notch.
On a length and outside off, Chandimal defends it off his back foot to complete the over.
The line from Curran is once again very straight and Mathews wristily works it behind square leg for a run.
Back of a length ball on off, Chandimal moves inside the line of the delivery and works it towards the square leg umpire for a single.
Fuller and on off, it's driven by Chandimal and it goes on one bounce to the silly mid off fielder.
Good length delivery on top of off, Chandimal defends it from the back foot and drops it with gentle hands in front of square on the off side.
A length delivery outside off, Chandimal walks across a bit and then withdraws his bat.
Fuller and on off, Mathews is forward in defense.
On a length and outside off, Mathews shoulders arms.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Fullish and on middle, prompting the batsman to play the flick shot, Mathews does that but finds the short mid-wicket fielder.
In a good channel outside off, that is left alone for the keeper to collect.
Good length delivery outside off, Mathews defends it to the off side from the back foot.

FOUR! On the pads and it's easy pickings for Dinesh Chandimal. Too full in length and the angle of the bowler further assisted the batsman. DC flicks it delightfully through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Uses the angle of the bowler and works a full ball on the leg side, picks out the short mid-wicket fielder.
Fuller and on off, Chandimal defends it off his front foot.
Back of a length ball on middle, Chandimal stays back and helps it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! That's more like it for Chandimal. It's a pitched up delivery outside off, Chandimal drives it crisply through extra cover to break the monotony of dot balls. A boundary.
A fuller length ball around off as Curran continues to run in from 'round the wicket with a silly mid off in place. Chandimal defends it to the off side.
Beaten this time! Great delivery by Jimmy! Lands it on a length and gets it to straighten outside off, Mathews ends up pushing and missing inside the line. Lack of footwork was quite evident there.
Stretches forward to a length ball outside off and defends it with soft hands to short cover.
Good length ball on off, Mathews moves back a bit and turns it on the leg side, finds short mid-wicket.
A bit short and around off, Angelo stays back-footed and defends it towards covers.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Slightly edgy! Anderson hurls in a length ball around off, a bit of extra bounce, Mathews pushes it with an angled bat and it comes off the outer portion. Rolls safely to the right of gully.
A good length ball, Chandimal works it with the angle of the bowler but finds the short mid-wicket fielder.
This one is on a length and outside off, DC makes a leave and pulls his bat just like Steven Smith does while leaving.
Angles in a full ball on off, Chandimal pushes it off his front foot to mid off, all along the ground.
The drive comes but it's well wide of that fielder and rolls to the fielder at covers.
A length ball on this occasion, Chandimal decides to stay back as he blocks it to the off side. There is a silly mid off in place waiting for an uppish drive.
Starts with a pitched up ball outside off, Chandimal pushes it off his front foot to covers.
Sam Curran is back on.
Good length delivery on off, Mathews stays back and defends it to the off side.
Around off, on a length and angling in, Mathews blocks it off his front foot.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Superb shot and a superb piece of fielding as well. Fuller length ball on middle, Mathews plays a well-timed on drive but Curran does well to make a diving stop by running across to his left.
A length delivery in the channel outside off, Mathews has nothing to do with it.
Flatter and outside off, Chandimal defends it to the off side.

MISFIELD AND FOUR! Flighted and full around off, Chandimal takes a step forward and forces his drive towards mid on. Looks for a run and Anderson charges across towards the ball to his left. Makes a complete mess as it goes through his legs and finds the fence. Bess is not impressed.
Tossed up ball around off, Chandimal pushes it off his front foot to covers.
A touch short around off, Dinesh helps it from the back foot to mid-wicket.
Flatter and quicker on middle, Chandimal moves back and defends it on the leg side.
Fullish and around off, Angelo walks down the track and knocks it down to long on for a run.
Dom Bess to continue from the other end.
Full and outside off, Anderson gets Chandimal driving there. It's straight to covers.
Nearly a drag on! A length ball close to off, Chandimal tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Chandimal shoulders arms on this occasion.
Fuller and on middle, a rare gift by Anderson, Chandimal tucks it through square leg for a couple of runs.
Skipper Dinesh Chandimal walks in next.

OUT! Caught behind! What a delivery, what a class bowler James Anderson is! He has managed to get something out of this unresponsive track. The English seamer speeds in from 'round the wicket and dishes out a length ball just outside off. It lands and straightens slightly, Thirimanne could have left it but he feels for it and tries to play at it outside the line of the stumps. Gets a thick outside edge and Buttler makes no mistake. Third wicket for Jimmy and he is turning out to be a true replacement for Stuart Broad. The partnership is broken and it's a great start for England after Lunch.
Hurls across a length ball outside off, Thirmanne gets forward and pushes it with an angled bat to cover-point.

We're back! The players are also back on the field as they get ready to kick off proceedings. England looked a bit flat in the last hour before Lunch as there wasn't much help from the pitch. They would try to keep things in control if the wickets are not falling and create pressure. For Sri Lanka, their sole aim will be to bat once and bat big and to achieve that, they have the best pair in the middle at the moment. Bright and sunny afternoon, the conditions are tailor-made for batting and another challenge for England will be to counter this sweltering heat. James Anderson to bowl first up...
..... DAY 1, SECOND SESSION .....

Right then. Looks like an even session based on the way that it has panned out. It will be interesting to see which side comes out looking to grab the second session. Will Thirimanne and Mathews continue on their merry way or will the bowling attack of the English Lions be able to breach their defenses? Join us for the second session in a short while at 1240 local (0710 GMT).

Just the start that the English Lions would have wanted to this session and Test. James Anderson, who was rested in the first Test, came back into this game and was right on the money. He removed two batters in the same over and provided the platform for the rest of the bowlers to follow suit. Although, the back-up bowlers found it tough to adjust to the conditions as there wasn't much assistance.

Another poor start by the Islanders. They lost two quick wickets in the 5th over as Kusal Perara played a very poor stroke and Fernando, going to get a feel of the ball, ended up chopping it back onto his stumps. Sri Lanka were reeling at 7/2 at the end of the 5th over but then a fantastic job of bringing some order into the batting was done by Thirimanne and Mathews, taking the hosts through the morning session unscathed. They have also added 69 runs to their stand and will be looking to build on this, come the second session.

A good, engaging first session of play comes to a close. You could say that England's noses are in front courtesy of the start that they got but a fine rebuilding job courtesy of Thirimanne and Mathews has seen Sri Lanka steady the ship after their streaky start.
Quicker one, fuller and flatter on off at 87 kph, Mathews draws forward and defends it solidly. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 1!
A tossed up ball landing outside off, Mathews pushes it from the back foot to covers.
Drags his length back and serves it around off, Thirimanne moves back and cuts it through point for a single.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out. Solid.
Bess bowls it full and around off, Lahiru lunges and defends it back.
Fuller and flatter on leg, Thirimanne forces it down to mid on.
Curran switches to 'round the wicket for the last ball and digs in a short ball on middle, Mathews ducks.
Slants in a fuller length ball on middle, Thirimanne this time tries to flick but it comes more from the inner portion of his blade. Goes aerial but in the gap at mid-wicket for a run.

Angling across the batsman around off, a little bit of extra bounce on this occasion, Mathews pushes at it with a loose bottom hand and it goes off the inner half. Rolls in front of square leg and they take a single.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.

FOUR! In the gap on this occasion! Curran once again bowls a fuller length ball around leg and middle, Mathews flicks it beautifully through the gap between mid-wicket and mid on. Angelo standing outside the crease is helping him in negating the movement, if any.
Starts his new spell with a fuller length ball on middle, Mathews, who is standing outside his crease, flicks it across the line but finds the short mid-wicket fielder.
Change of bowler just at the stroke of the Lunch Break. Sam Curran (4-1-14-0) is reintroduced into the attack.
Uses his feet to get down the track to a full ball and eases it through mid on for a comfortable single.
Quicker and flatter on middle, Mathews works it off his pads to short mid-wicket.
Shortish and on off, it's punched in the gap at covers for a run.
Fuller and on off, Thirimanne defends it back off his front foot.
Knocks a full ball down through mid on for a run.

England are not happy with the shape of the ball. They have convinced the umpires it appears and the ball is getting changed. Scratch that, the update is that the umpires have not changed the ball. The halt in the play was due to Mathews who changed his bat.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
FOUR! Superb shot! Thirimanne's batting has been a nice blend of intent and defense. Fuller and around off, Thirimanne goes with the turn and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
A good diving stop! Full and floated around off, Thirimanne drives it off his front foot but Bairstow does well to stop it with a dive at covers.
A firm drive down the ground. Too full and on middle, Angelo picks up a single after sending the ball towards mid off.
Flighted and around off, Thirimanne plays a defensive push at covers, it's in the gap and they take a run.
Presses forward to a full ball on middle and blocks it back in the direction of the bowler.
Plays it nice and in the V, risk-free! Fuller and on off, Mathews drives it through mid off for an easy run.
Fullish and around leg, Lahiru uses his wrists but finds short leg with his attempted flick shot.
Drags his length short around off, Thirimanne cuts it from the back foot to point.
Quicker one, flatter and on middle at 92 kph, Thirimanne moves back inside the crease in defense.
Nicely tossed up ball on off, Thirimanne defends it with gentle hands to short leg.
Flighted and on middle and off, from 'round the wicket, Lahiru defends it off his front foot.
Shortish and on off, turning in a bit, Mathews hangs back and punches it down to long on for a run.
A tossed up ball landing full around off, Thirimanne lunges and defends it right under his watchful eyes.
This time Mathews finds the gap. A slightly short ball around off, Angelo moves back and forces it through the gap at covers for one.
Full and around off, Mathews pushes it gently to short cover.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! 50-run stand comes up! Some extra loop on this delivery but it's very full on the pads, Mathews picks it up and whips it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Good recovery from Sri Lanka after losing two early wickets.
Flighted delivery on the pads, it's worked in the gap at mid-wicket for a run. A nice wristy shot by Lahiru.
Leans forward to meet the fuller length ball on middle and defends it to the off side.
A touch short around off, Thirimanne goes back and pushes it through covers for a run. Not much spin so far.
Loopy and full on off, slower in air, Lahiru presses forward and defends it back.
Flatter and short around off, a slider, Thirimanne cuts it from the back foot but finds point.
Loopy and full on off, Thirimanne leans forward to defend but it takes the inner half and rolls to short leg.
Good shot! Slightly short and around leg, spinning further down, Mathews nudges it past Leach at short fine leg. He pulls it back before the rope and they take three runs. 50 up for Sri Lanka.
Leach drags his length short and serves it around off, Mathews moves back and punches it in front of square on the off side for one. This pair has been largely untroubled so far.
A tossed up ball landing full on off, Angelo jams it out safely off the front foot.
Flatter and a touch short around off, Mathews gets back with the square cut but finds point.
Gets forward to a full ball again and pushes it with the spin, if any, to short cover.
Floated and full around off, Mathews lunges and defends it to short cover.
Starts his new spell from the opposite end and bowls a full ball on the leg stump line, Lahiru flicks it in front of square leg for a run.
Change of ends for Jack Leach. 4-1-16-0 are his numbers so far.
Flatter and around off, Lahiru nudges this around the corner to exchange ends. Good start from Bess. Just one off his first over.
On off, nudged to the leg side.
Flighted and on off, Lahiru drives this one to the cover region.
Flatter and around off, worked to the point region.
Flighted around off, pushed to covers again, where the fielder makes a good stop.
Short and around off, punched to covers.
It is time for some off spin from Dom Bess! Five wickets in the first innings of the first Test match, can he do the same?
Around the off pole, tucked to the fielder present at mid-wicket. A dot to finish a strong over from Wood.
On the pads, Thirimanne clips this one behind square on the leg side and he crosses ends with Angelo.
Another loud 'NOOOO' from Lahiru. Short of a length and on middle, he jumps and negotiates this one out to the leg side.
Another length delivery around the off pole, Lahiru drives this one but it is straight to the mid on fielder. Says no again for the single.
Slightly short and around off, LT hops and keeps it out.
Around off, length, pushed to point. No single this time as Lahiru is clear in communicating his decision to stay put.
Flighted and around off, Lahiru backs away and cuts this one to deep point for a single. 7 off this over. Leach has been on the expensive start at the moment.
On off, kept out.

FOUR! Thirimanne is slowly building his score now. Very well played. Flighted and around off, Lahiru stays put and drives this one through the cover region. Jimmy Anderson gives it chase but he comes second in the race to the ropes.
Flighted on off, blocked.
On middle, tucked to the leg side.
Loopy around off, Lahiru drives this one through the cover region. Picks up a couple.
The physio is out in the middle now. Having a look at Thirimanne's hand as he seems to be slightly uncomfortable. All good to go as he gets ready to face the next ball.
Good length, around the off pole, Angelo negotiates this one safely to see off the over.
Slightly shorter and on the body, Lahiru works this one to deep square leg. Takes a single.
On off, pushed to the mid on region.
Length and around off and middle, LT clips this one through the square leg region. By the time the fielder can clean up in the deep, two runs are taken.
Back of a length and on middle, Lahiru this time decides to take it on as he hops and flicks this one to the mid-wicket region. Went straight to the fielder, so no run will be possible.
Spicy bumper on middle, Lahiru ducks under this one.
Flighted on leg, Angelo pushes this to short leg. 6 off this one. Sri Lanka are trying to be positive against the spinner.
Short and around middle, tucked to the leg side. One run.
Tossed up and around off, Lahiru keeps this one out.
Short and around off, punched to deep cover for a single.
FOUR! Mathews now taking the charge to the bowler. Flighted and around off, Mathews just lofts this one over the mid off region and the ball bounces before crossing the ropes.
Floated around off, blocked.

DRINKS. Just the start that the visitors would have been looking for. 2 quick wickets to their name and now Sri Lanka are on the back foot. England would be looking to scalp a couple more wickets before the Lunch break as that would put them in the ascendancy. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, have had yet another poor start. Thirimanne and Mathews will be hoping to fend off any other challenge until the Break.
On off, pushed to the mid on region.
Wood comes 'round the wicket this time and angles in a length delivery around off and middle, Lahiru nudges this one to the leg side.
Length and around off, punched towards point, but this time, to the fielder present there.

FOUR! SHOT! Just waits for it and then dispatches this one. Fuller and around off, Thirimanne leans into this one and creams the drive through the extra cover region and the ball speeds away to the ropes. Top shot!
Outside off, Thirimanne is watchful as he lets this one through to the keeper.
Around the off pole, Lahiru plays this to point. Denies the single on this occasion.
Goes fuller and around middle again, tucked towards mid-wicket but Angelo finds the fielder present there. Maiden from Leach.
Flighted on middle, Mathews blocks towards mid on.
Fuller and around off, kept out.
Now comes on his front foot and blocks this one out.
Flighted around middle and leg, nudged to short leg by Angelo.
On middle, played to covers.
Back of a length and around off, LT pushes this one to the cover region. Only 2 runs off Wood's first over.
Gets his bat down and blocks. Thirimanne has been very solid in his defensive strokes, so far.
Mathews pushes this one towards the leg side for a single.
Slight movement noticed from Wood. Length and around off, nips back in just about after hitting the deck, Angelo blocks this one out.
Length and around off, Lahiru taps this one towards point. 'YEAH, YEAH, YEAHHH', says Thirimanne for the single and they complete it with ease, in the end.
Starts with a good length delivery outside off, Thirimanne leaves it be.
Change from both ends. Mark Wood to speed in now. He caused some problems to Mathews in the first Test. Will be interesting to see that battle again.
Loopy and around off, Angelo watches the ball spin away from him and just lets it be. A good start by Leach.
Short and on middle, Lahiru flicks this one to deep square leg. One more run.
Short and wide outside off, Angelo punches this one to the deep cover region. Rotates ends.
Flighted and around off, nudged to the leg side for a single.
Slightly behind the fuller length and around off, spins back in again, LT goes on his back foot and works this to short leg again.
Floated around off, spins back in slightly, Lahiru tucks this one to the fielder present at short leg.
Looks like it is time for some spin. Dom Bess was warming up but it was a false alarm. Jack Leach is the first bowling change. A slip and short leg in place.
Takes the single on the last ball. Slightly behind the good length and around middle, Thirimanne hops and nudges this one to the deep backward square leg region. Retains the strike for the next over.
On off, length delivery, kept out.
Dom Bess is warming up.
Just testing the waters, is Lahiru. Length and around the off pole, Thirimanne pushes this one towards mid on again.
Good length and around off, Lahiru gets his bat ahead and defends it out.
Good length, around off, worked to the mid on region.
Prods on his front foot and defends this good length delivery out solidly.
Goes slightly fuller and around off, LT works this one to the deep mid-wicket region. Picks up a single.
Drags his length back, does Sam. A shortish length ball on middle, Lahiru just sits under this one.
On a good length and around middle, Thirimanne tucks this one to the mid-wicket region. 'NOOOOO', says Lahiru, in regard to the single.
Back of a length delivery around off, Thirimanne pushes this one towards covers.
Outside off, left alone.
Blocked out solidly by Lahiru. This was on a good length just around the off stump.
Single on the last ball. Length and on middle, clipped to the deep square leg region for one.
Gets his bat down in time and fends this one out again, Thirimanne.
Short of a length delivery around off, Lahiru, again keeps a straight bat and defends this one out.
This time, Lahiru shuffles and keeps this one out well.
Outside off on a good length, left alone.
Fuller length and around off, Lahiru puts his right foot ahead and raises his blade to let this one through to the keeper.
On the pads, tucked to the leg side. 9 off this over. A good one for the hosts.
BEATEN! Good bowling by Sam. Length and around off, angling across the right-hander, Mathews comes ahead and looks to block this one out but the ball misses the outside edge and goes to the keeper.
Good length delivery and around off, Angelo just taps this one towards point. Not going to risk a single, are these two. Not after this start, at least.
LEG BYE. Back of a length and on the pads, Lahiru hops and looks to tuck but he misses and the ball takes the pad and rolls to the leg side. A leg bye is sneaked in.

EDGY FOUR! Ohhh...could have been a goner this time, Lahiru. A length ball, outside off, nips away slightly, Thirimanne looks to punch this to the off side but the ball takes the outside edge and flies in between the slip region and gully fielder, into the third man fence for another boundary.
FOUR! A welcome boundary for the Lankans after their last over. Curran goes slightly straighter and on the pads, Thirimanne just tickles this one to the fine leg region for a boundary.
Fuller length ball on off, Mathews covers the line and movement before offering a straight bat in defense. A double-wicket maiden!
Sri Lanka lose another. In some trouble now as they are 2 down in the first 5 overs. Can someone come in and steady the ship? Angelo Mathews is the new batter in.

OUT! Drags it on! Another wicket down in the 5th over and Anderson is on fire. Back of a length delivery outside off, Fernando stands back to push at it but there is some extra bounce. It takes the inner half of his bat and cannons onto his stumps. The batsman can consider himself unlucky but he had no business hanging his bat so wide away from his body. Poor technique. Yet another sorry start for Sri Lanka.
Lands it on a length and close to off, Fernando pushes it with an angled bat to point.
In the corridor of uncertainty, the batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
That is left alone for the keeper to collect.
Early blow for the Lankans. Who comes in now? Oshada Fernando is in at Number 3.

OUT! Caught at first slip! Poor, poor shot by Kusal Perera. Anderson angles in a fuller length ball around off from 'round the wicket, Perera attempts to probably heave it over the leg side but gets a big fat edge behind. Joe Root jumps and completes the catch over his head. On a closer look at the replays, there wasn't enough movement but the seam of the delivery was pointing towards the slip cordon. So maybe, that made the ball to nip away a shade, very little. Questionable shot selection by Kusal Perera, you can say that he bats this way but that doesn't cover up the fact that it was a very substandard shot selection. You cannot just plant your front foot and hit across the line in the first 30 minutes of a Test match.

Once again, this shot is not middled. Curran gets it to move away from around off, after landing on a fuller length, Perera tries to flick but it takes the inside half and rolls to square leg. A single is taken.

FOUR! First of this Test match! Curran delivers it full and outside off, Perera goes hard at it and forces it back past the bowler and his partner for a boundary at long on. Not from the middle of the bat, that!

Curran is probably trying for a magic delivery. But is not getting the desired movement. Hurls a full ball around middle and leg and it goes down with the angle. Perera fails to flick and it's a good stop by Buttler.
This time the line is a bit too straight as the ball doesn't move, Perera calmly keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Curran is a smart operator! Gets close to the stumps on this occasion, moving away a bit off the seam, Perera tries to work it around but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Curran is getting some movement going! He manages to make a curve away from the left-hander as he dishes out a full length just outside off, Perera shoulders arms.
Angles in a full ball around off for Kusal Perera, it's bowled from 'round the wicket, KP drops it with gentle hands to covers and pinches a run to open his account.
Sri Lanka are away in the third over! Good length ball outside off, Thirimmane taps it down towards covers and steals a run.

A nervous moment for Lahiru! He defends a length ball from the back foot as there is some extra bounce. It thuds on his bat and then starts to roll behind. Thirimanne reacts, looks back but the ball is away from the stumps.
On a length and outside off, that is left alone for the keeper to collect.
Movement back into the left-hander, very slightly, Thirimanne closes the face of his bat in defense as he pushes it to mid-wicket.
Good length ball on off, it's blocked from the crease by Thirimanne.
Beaten! Fuller in length and around off, Perera prods forward to defend but it moves away slightly to beat the outside edge. Top first over by Sam!
In the channel outside off, left alone by Perera.
Back of a length delivery on off, Perera stays back to push it towards covers.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.

NOT OUT! Kusal Perera survives a scare. Beauty of a delivery by Sam Curran! He got some movement on the first ball and immediately changed his line to middle and leg. He manages to straighten it from there and Kusal fails to work it around. He's trapped on the pads, the appeal goes up but the finger stays down. Joe Root opts for the DRS as it looked plumb to the naked eye. All the protocols of the DRS are followed, Ultra Edge and Ball Tracker take some time to generate but eventually come to the rescue of the third umpire and show that Perera is safe as it's the umpire's call.

Huge shout for an lbw! That looked out to the naked eye. But it's not given and Joe Root takes the DRS. No bat as confirmed by the Ultra Edge. Time for the Ball Tracker - It's clipping the leg stump. Umpire's call!
Some movement first up for Curran. He angles it on a fuller length around off, shaping away slightly, Perera covers everything before defending it from the back foot.
This time Anderson pitches it further up, almost on a driving length it's served, Thirimanne though is not getting lured so early. He isn't Kusal Perera.
Who will partner Anderson with the new ball, from the other end? Sam Curran, it will be.
A better line from Jimmy! Delivers it on a length and very close to off, Thirimanne makes another leave as it goes on with the angle.
The length is slightly up than the last time but the line is still outside off, Thirimanne is very watchful in his leave.
Good length delivery on off, angling across the left-handed batsman, Lahiru shoulders arms and it's a good carry to Buttler.
A touch short and around middle and off, Thirimanne stands back to turn it on the leg side. Not in the gap as the square leg fielder gets into the act.
Starts with a back of a length ball, it lands around leg and angles across towards off, Thirimanne is firmly behind the line in defense.

Right then. We are done with all the pre-match formalities as the action is all set to begin. The players of England are already out on the field and are looking to spread out to their respective positions out on the field. The are followed by the Sri Lankan openers, Kusal Perera and Lahiru Thirimanne. James Anderson to begin with the ball for the visitors. Here he comes....

Pitch report - It's very humid out there! They are using a different pitch and it looks a lot better for batting. It will have good bounce and carry at the same time, reckons Russel Arnold who also feels that it won't turn from Day 1. Application is going to be the key.

Captains' thoughts - Sri Lankan skipper, Dinesh Chandimal said at the toss that they have reflected on their performance in the last Test match and are eager to do well as a team. He talked about having some plans up their sleeves which they would like to execute when the situation will come. Joe Root, on the other hand, praised his team for a fantastic first Test and told that they know it is going to be a different challenge and they are ready for it. Mentioned that they are full of confidence and would love to transfer that into a win.
England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Dom Sibley, Jonny Bairstow, Joe Root (C), Daniel Lawrence, Jos Buttler (WK), Sam Curran, Dom Bess, Jack Leach, Mark Wood, James Anderson (In for Stuart Broad).

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Lahiru Thirimanne, Kusal Perera, Oshada Fernando (In for Kusal Mendis), Dinesh Chandimal (C), Angelo Mathews, Niroshan Dickwella (WK), Ramesh Mendis (In for Dasun Shanaka), Dilruwan Perera, Suranga Lakmal (In for Wanindu Hasaranga), Lasith Embuldeniya, Asitha Fernando.

It's toss time now! Joe Root calls it wrongly and Dinesh Chandimal makes the most obvious decision - SRI LANKA ELECT TO BAT! It's confirmed that Ramesh Mendis will make his Test debut and will become the 154th player to represent Sri Lanka in this format. England, on the other hand, had announced their XI last evening, making one change - resting Stuart Broad and including James Anderson in his place.

Pitch and conditions! The venue remains the same so both teams know what to expect. This time around it's a lot drier unlike the last occasion and hence you can expect a typical subcontinent pitch. Needless to say, toss is going to play a big part as no one would want to bat last here. That's a normal template mainly for the touring teams to bat first and bat big, if possible, to give themselves an outside chance against the mighty hosts. However, things are slightly different in this series with Sri Lanka not at their dominant best, still, you can expect the template to remain the same.

Confidence and momentum rest with the touring team. They will be dreaming about a back-to-back series win in the Island nation but should be ready for a backlash. Sri Lanka started their comeback from the last Test match only as in the latter half, they were way better than the opening day mishap. So, it's going to be a battle between on-song England and hurt but resurging Sri Lanka. Should be a cracking contest!

Hello, folks! Welcome to Galle 2.0. First Test match turned out to be the story of one bad batting innings from the home team and they had to pay for it throughout. It had a ripple effect and effected their bowling too as England rode the momentum and Root's extraordinary knock shut the door on the face of Sri Lanka. To repeat the same, the Three Lions will step out again and let's see how the Lankan Lions respond this time around. Stay tuned for more...
